history.summary: Bhagavathy temple at Cherthala, one of the 108 Durga temples of Kerala, whose deity was consecrated per legend by the saint Vilwamangalam Swamiyar. The Devi is worshipped as a swayambhu shila set nearly 4 feet below ground level, darshanam facing east, with a gold-plated flagpost and daily sheeveli. Legend: the saint chased a maiden (the Devi) through seven ponds and installed her on the banks of Karuppankulam; the name 'Cherthala' is linked to 'cher' (mud) and 'thala' (head). She is venerated as Mangalya Dayini, remover of marriage obstacles, with famous offerings Iratti, Thadi and Kalabham. Note: built-date claims conflict — one source says 17th century by Marthanda Varma, another 16th century by a ruler 'Karthikyan', the temple website ~1,080 years — none verified.

name: Karthyayani Devi Temple
town_description: Cherthala is a coastal municipal town in Alappuzha district, about 22 km north of Alappuzha and 40 km south of Kochi on NH66. Historically Cherthalai, it is a major centre of Kerala's coir industry and is also known for its white-sand coastline and backwaters, and as the birthplace of statesman A. K. Antony. The town is well connected by road and rail, with Cochin International Airport the nearest airport.
